purpose: Canonical public-safe family ownership, dependency, governance, maintainability, AI-navigation, and change contract for the two active Z-Solo-King repositories.

owns: public Worker boundary and public readiness
public CI and public-safe regression coverage
promotion, canary, rollback and release authority
must_not_own: a second implementation of a Foundation-owned public deterministic primitive
a second authoritative public contract definition

dependency.rule: Foundation public/runtime code never depends on Operations source, private credentials, private runtime state, or protected implementation. The only allowed Foundation -> Operations source relationship is a protected GitHub Actions maintenance/deployment bridge that executes a purpose-specific private utility from an immutable verified Operations revision.
dependency.implementation_rule: Operations may consume a pinned Foundation package/revision. Cross-repository reuse must use a versioned contract or the canonical Foundation package, never copy-paste source.

requirements: workflow must run only from protected main and an approved protected environment
private source must be addressed by an immutable Operations commit SHA
access must use the purpose-specific GitHub App with least-privilege repository scope
private source must not be copied into the public repository or artifacts
secret values must remain environment-bound and absent from logs/artifacts
bridge must not become a second application runtime or policy authority

single_owner_rule.rule: Each behavior, policy, data model, registry, algorithm, and authority has exactly one canonical owner.
single_owner_rule.compatibility: Compatibility modules may re-export or adapt a canonical implementation but must contain no second business algorithm or policy.
single_owner_rule.generated_code: Generated output is never a source of truth.
single_owner_rule.legacy_code: Historical snapshots are immutable references and cannot receive new business logic.

placement_rules.rule: Place code by responsibility, lifecycle, trust boundary, dependency direction, and testing ownership rather than by convenience or historical filename.
foundation_when: behavior is public-safe and reusable without private credentials or protected policy
behavior is deterministic and stable enough to serve multiple private consumers
the contract must remain independently testable in public CI
operations_when: behavior requires protected policy, credentials, private topology, acquisition, private adapters, private evaluation, promotion, recovery, or orchestration
behavior is experimental, provider-specific, site-specific, or operationally volatile
behavior must remain private for trust or security reasons
split_module_when: two responsibilities have different owners, lifecycle, trust boundary, or test strategy
a module becomes difficult to reason about because unrelated policies or side effects share one execution path
splitting materially reduces change risk without creating another authority
do_not_split_when: the split would create artificial wrappers with no independent responsibility
it would duplicate shared state or force repeated orchestration between tiny files
the only benefit is shorter files rather than clearer ownership
move_between_repositories_when: the current repository violates the ownership boundary
the code can be relocated without exposing protected behavior or breaking a required public contract
parity/regression evidence proves the new owner is complete before the old implementation is removed

principles: small cohesive modules rather than arbitrary fragmentation
side effects isolated from deterministic logic
compatibility shims remain thin and temporary
tests live with the owner and at cross-repository boundaries
historical code is immutable or clearly archived
comments explain why and constraints, not obvious syntax
every important subsystem has a compact machine-readable navigation entry
Machine-readable schemas and authority maps are sources of truth; human-facing documentation should reference them rather than duplicate mutable values.
change_safety: change one canonical owner at a time
preserve rollback and recovery semantics for side effects
re-run affected boundary tests after moving code
remove old paths after parity evidence instead of carrying permanent duplicate implementations

ai_navigation.goal: Make human and AI maintenance efficient, accurate, and low-token by resolving ownership before reading implementation detail.
navigation_order: only then broader repository search when required
token_efficiency: prefer compact indexes, hashes, typed contracts, and bounded context over repeated full-file scans
retrieve only the architecture fragments relevant to the current task
do not copy repository documentation into runtime prompts when a canonical path/reference is sufficient
deduplicate repeated evidence before model reasoning under an explicit budget
separate navigation metadata from implementation payloads
use deterministic filters before semantic/model comparison
accuracy: never infer ownership from filename similarity when a canonical map exists
distinguish source of truth from compatibility/export paths
treat model knowledge as potentially stale for volatile facts
do not claim tool, file, repository, or execution access without evidence
preserve provenance and uncertainty across transformations
Never resurrect retired AI_CODEMAP.json as a runtime or navigation authority; use REPOSITORY_MAP.json plus the canonical family registry.
Treat exact public release pins and private utility pins as purpose-scoped immutable evidence, not mutable branch references.

boundary_rules: Public source code must not reveal private credentials, private topology, private holdouts, or protected implementation details.
Mapping remains network-free; acquisition/network work belongs to Operations acquisition/execution paths.
Family-level resource accounting has one authority in operations/private/resource_ledger.py.
Family-level promotion authority has one owner in Operations.
Public readiness must work without the private control plane.
Operations may add stricter local fail-closed guards, but local guards must not become competing family policy authorities.
The retired extractor-mapper repository is historical material only and cannot become a third active ownership boundary.

Privileged public workflows may execute approved private utilities only through an immutable Operations revision verified at runtime; the public tree must contain the bridge contract, not the private implementation.
change_method: classify the requested behavior, policy, model, or contract
resolve the canonical owner from this contract and the repository codemap
inspect the existing implementation and consumers before adding code
extend the owner instead of creating a peer implementation
expose the smallest stable versioned contract needed by the consumer
add boundary coverage when the change crosses repositories
run the family overlap/ownership audit when structure or ownership changes
remove obsolete compatibility or duplicate implementations after parity evidence
update this contract plus the affected codemap when ownership or dependency direction changes
for maintenance/refactor requests, re-check placement, duplication, side effects, and AI navigation before declaring completion

duplication_policy.optimization: Deep pairwise comparison is for periodic exhaustive audits; routine checks should use deterministic hashing, structural bucketing, dependency/ownership indexes, and targeted expensive comparison.
duplication_policy.no_false_merge: Similarity alone never authorizes merging. Ownership, behavior, side effects, trust boundary, and compatibility requirements must also agree.

validation.foundation: Public CI validates public-safe contracts, deterministic primitives, boundary behavior, and security-relevant public paths.
validation.operations: Private validation is local, private-self-hosted, or another non-GitHub-hosted path and validates protected runtime, evaluation, promotion, and deployment behavior.
validation.family: Cross-repository overlap and ownership audits are run from Operations as the protected family control plane.

non_negotiable: no copy-paste across repositories for shared behavior
no duplicate deterministic public-core algorithm in Operations
no new code in immutable legacy snapshots
no hidden third active repository or ownership boundary
architecture knowledge must reference canonical source rather than become a second architecture database
protected workflow bridges may consume private Operations utilities only under the explicit immutable-handoff rule; public application/runtime code may not import private Operations source.
